mappings.basis: Unit 7 states that the proposal is exempt under RCW 34.05.310(4) or 34.05.330(1); its evidence [111,172] covers the target quote and the R1 clause. Same actor (the proposal), same assertion (is exempt), same modality.

Unit 41 states that the rule is exempt from the RCW 34.05.328 requirements including a cost-benefit analysis, i.e. the implied target (those requirements apply) does not hold for the named exempted thing, this rule. Evidence [3211,3456] overlaps the target quote and the R2 clause.

Unit 42 states that the proposal or portions of it are exempt from the Regulatory Fairness Act, denying the implied target for the named population; evidence overlaps the target quote and the R3 clause. Unit 46 states that the rule proposal is fully exempt, restating the exemption for the whole proposal; evidence [4064,4120] overlaps the R4 clause.

mapping_doubts.note: inverse vs opposite is close: the exempted thing (this rule) is the same object the gloss names, so the unit could be read as a flat denial. Chose inverse because the unit names the exempted thing and the circumstance (content dictated by statute), matching the "X is exempt from Y" pattern in question 2.

Unit 46 does not itself name the Regulatory Fairness Act; what the rule proposal is fully exempt from is supplied only by the enclosing block. Mapped inverse because the reference attaches R4 to T3 on the same basis and a reader of the unit with its evidence takes it as the scope of that exemption. A stricter reading would leave unit 46 unmapped.
Unit 7 hedges with "is reported exempt"; treated as attribution wording, not a change in modality direction.

other: Units 43, 44 and 45 restate the Explanation of exemptions (statutory mandates), not the applicability of the Regulatory Fairness Act, so they do not map to T3.
No unit separately asserts "A cost-benefit analysis is not required under RCW 34.05.328"; unit 41 evidence spans that sentence but its assertion is only the exemption statement.
